messages.body_plain:
thanks to nick locantore, renaud lancelot, andy liaw, s.d. byers,
charles c. berry, frank herrell, and gérald jean for their quick and
helpful answers. they are quite different, but all of work (by using the
function cut or cut2). here their application on a simple data frame.

bernd

library(Hmisc, T)

x <- data.frame(1:10)
x$quar1 <- cut2(x$X1.10, g=4)
x$quar2 <- cut(x$X1.10, breaks=quantile(x$X1.10), include.lowest=T)
x$quar3 <- cut(x$X1.10, breaks = quantile(x$X1.10, prob = seq(0, 1,
1/4)))
x$quar4 <- factor( cut( x$X1.10,
breaks=quantile(x$X1.10,probs=(0:4)/4)+c(-0.001, rep(0,4-1),0.001 ) ))
x$quar5 <- cut(x$X1.10, quantile(x$X1.10, seq(from=0, to = 1, by =
0.25)),include.lowest = TRUE )
x$quar6 <-  cut(x$X1.10, breaks = quantile(x$X1.10), include.lowest = T,
 factor.result = T, labels = c('1st quart.', '2nd quart.', '3rd quart.',
'4th quart.'))

messages.subject: summary - nested effects in REGLM
messages.body_plain:
Thank you to Brian Ripley, Renaud Lancelot and 
Gordon Smyth for their advice on REGLM and LME.

 

My question was whether anybody had experience 
incorporating nested random effects into the REGLM function (generalized linear 
models with random effects, as described in the S-Archive).  The linear 
mixed-effects models do not currently accommodate overdispersed or binomial 
data.

(1991) method, allows additive random effects, but may not be stable for 
nested effects. B. Ripley and R. Lancelot suggested that the "glmmPQL " 
function (R version) in the MASS library could be used to model nested 
random effects.  B. Ripley also mentioned that the upcoming GLME from Jose' 
Pinheiro would do the same

messages.subject: GUI Graphics Crashes Resolved
messages.body_plain:
I previously complained on this list of repeated crashes when using GUI 
graphics in S-Plus 6.0 Professional. Recently, I made a change that 
eliminated those crashes in the cases I have tried so far.

A local computer guru suggested examining the "AGP Graphics Aperture" 
setting in the BIOS of the PC. It had been set (presumably by the system 
vendor) to 256Mb on a machine with 512Mb of memory, and we reduced it to 
32Mb.  The formerly problematic S-Plus operations now run fine.

I can't claim to understand what that setting is, why it was set so high, 
or why reducing it helped, nor have I used the new setting long enough to 
say it has eliminated all such crashes.  Nonetheless, it has made a huge 
difference in stability so far.

--
Michael Prager      <Mike.Prager at noaa.gov>
NOAA Center for Coastal Fisheries and Habitat Research
Beaufort, North Carolina  28516  USA

messages.subject: missing factor levels and trellis panel.superpose
messages.subject_clean: missing factor levels and trellis panel.superpose
messages.body_plain:
Time again for my once-a-year post to this invaluable list.

I'm in the process of modifying panel.superpose for plotting chulls 
for the groups=variable and noticed the following behaviour. Not 
sure if it's a bug, would appreciate any advice. 

The basic problem is that if there is a missing group level in one 
of the panels, panel=panel.superpose seems to keep track of and 
retain the correct plotting symbols, whereas calling panel.superpose 
from within panel=function(etc) seems to mess up the symbol order.

See the code below for example. I'm using SP2000 rel3 on W98.

dat <- data.frame(J = factor(rep(sort(rep(letters[1:3],4)),4)), 
        K = factor(rep( LETTERS[1:4], rep(12,4))), x = rep(1:12,4), 
        y = rnorm(48))

# everything looks OK
xyplot(y~x|K,groups=J,data=dat,
panel=panel.superpose,
key=list(transparent=T, columns=3, 
points=Rows(trellis.par.get("superpose.symbol"), 1:3),
, text=list(levels(dat$J))))

# different way to call, but everything still looks OK
xyplot(y~x|K,groups=J,data=dat,subscripts=T,
        panel=function(x,y,groups,subscripts,...){
                panel.superpose(x,y,groups,subscripts,...)},    
key=list(transparent=T, columns=3, 
points=Rows(trellis.par.get("superpose.symbol"), 1:3),
, text=list(levels(dat$J))))

# drop group b from the variable J where K=B
dat2<-dat[-c(17:20),]

# redo the first way, everything looks OK
xyplot(y~x|K,groups=J,data=dat2,
panel=panel.superpose,
key=list(transparent=T, columns=3, 
points=Rows(trellis.par.get("superpose.symbol"), 1:3),
, text=list(levels(dat$J))))

# redo the second way, and for panel K=B the pch 
# for J=c is replaced by the symbol for the missing level J=b
xyplot(y~x|K,groups=J,data=dat2,subscripts=T,
        panel=function(x,y,groups,subscripts,...){
                panel.superpose(x,y,groups,subscripts,...)},    
key=list(transparent=T, columns=3, 
points=Rows(trellis.par.get("superpose.symbol"), 1:3),
, text=list(levels(dat$J))))

Things get really hairy when you have many levels to the grouping
variable and multiple missing levels in an individual panel. 
I've been trawling through panel.superpose but I suspect I may 
have to attack some of the other trellis functions. (If indeed
it is a problem at all)

Thanks in advance,

John McKinlay
